conclusion: On this Windows Ninja build, adding data members to GCode.hpp does not trigger recompilation of every direct consumer. A stale Print.cpp.obj allocates GCode with the old class size, which corrupts members and can surface as an access violation in m_skirt_group_done.clear() during GCode::do_export. Rebuild GCode.cpp, Print.cpp, calib.cpp and BeltGCode.cpp together after changing GCode.hpp; do not misattribute this build-ABI failure to the organic support stage named by the last flushed log line.

verification.summary: The stale Print.cpp.obj predated GCode.hpp by hours and Ninja reported zero dependencies for it. Disassembly showed invalid vector state at m_skirt_group_done.clear(). After rebuilding Print.cpp, calib.cpp, BeltGCode.cpp and GCode.cpp, the same test.3mf completed G-code export instead of exiting with code 2816.
